sources.author: Harrison Chase
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO @ LangChain
sources.post_summary: Discussed the rapid evolution of AI agents, highlighting how multi-agent systems are moving from research to production. Shared insights on infrastructure challenges and the need for better orchestration tools for developers building reliable agents.

sources.author: Simon Willison
sources.headline: Co-creator of Datasette, AI & Python tooling advocate
sources.post_summary: Explored how AI tooling is reshaping developer workflows, focusing on automation of repetitive coding tasks. Emphasized the importance of open-source infrastructure to avoid vendor lock-in in AI development stacks.

sources.author: Sarah Guo
sources.headline: Founder @ Conviction, AI investor & operator
sources.post_summary: Analyzed the current state of AI infrastructure, noting that compute and data pipelines remain the biggest bottlenecks. Shared observations on emerging startups building agent-specific infrastructure layers.

sources.author: Matt Rickard
sources.headline: Founder @ Replicate, AI infrastructure
sources.post_summary: Posted about practical lessons deploying AI agents at scale, including monitoring, cost control, and reliability. Highlighted new developer tools that simplify agent evaluation and debugging.

sources.author: Alex Hormozi
sources.headline: Founder @ Acquisition.com | Author of $100M Offers
sources.post_summary: Discussed building outbound systems that scale without burning leads, emphasizing the need for precise targeting and automated follow-up sequences. Highlighted how content strategy should feed directly into outbound to warm up prospects before sales touches.

sources.author: Elena Verna
sources.headline: Growth Advisor | Former CMO @ Amplitude, Webflow
sources.post_summary: Shared a framework for aligning content strategy with revenue operations by mapping content assets to specific stages of the buyer journey. Argued that GTM engineering requires tight integration between marketing content and sales sequences.

sources.author: Harry Stebbings
sources.headline: Founder @ 20VC | Investor
sources.post_summary: Explored how modern sales ops teams are using automation to reduce CAC while maintaining personalization at scale. Covered tooling choices and the importance of clean data infrastructure for outbound automation.

sources.author: David Cancel
sources.headline: Founder @ Drift | CEO @ Toast
sources.post_summary: Talked about building GTM engineering functions that treat sales and marketing as a single revenue system. Emphasized using data loops from content engagement to refine outbound targeting and improve conversion rates.

sources.author: April Dunford
sources.headline: Positioning Expert | Author of Obviously Awesome
sources.post_summary: Explained how positioning and content strategy should drive outbound automation rather than generic sequences. Shared examples of how sales ops teams can use positioning frameworks to create more effective, context-aware outreach.

sources.author: Arjun Mahadevan
sources.headline: Founder & CEO at SuperOps | Ex-Freshworks
sources.post_summary: Shared the journey of pivoting from a services mindset to building a product-led SaaS company. Highlighted how early customer conversations shaped the MVP and why shipping weekly iterations helped them gain traction without a large team.

sources.author: Daniel Vassallo
sources.headline: Independent maker | Author of The Good Life in the 21st Century
sources.post_summary: Posted about his experience as a solo founder shipping multiple small products. Discussed the tradeoffs of staying solo vs hiring, and how he uses public updates to stay accountable and attract early users.

sources.author: Sara Mauskopf
sources.headline: Co-founder & CEO at Winnie | Mom of 3
sources.post_summary: Wrote about transitioning from a corporate PM role into founding a startup. Shared the emotional side of the career pivot and how consistent public updates helped her build an audience and find early customers.

sources.author: Pieter Levels
sources.headline: Indie maker | Founder of Nomad List, Remote OK
sources.post_summary: Shared a thread on shipping 12+ products as a solo developer over the years. Focused on the importance of launching fast, learning from real usage data, and maintaining transparency with his audience.

sources.author: Vic Vijayakumar
sources.headline: Founder at Replit | Ex-Google
sources.post_summary: Talked about the early days of building Replit as a solo project while working full-time. Emphasized how public progress updates helped him get feedback and eventually attract co-founders and investors.
